title: Senior asks: someone posts a JSON array nested 600 levels deep. decodeJson() uses json_decode(..., true). What does it return?
options: null (the default depth is 512), so the user sees 'Invalid JSON.'
explain: json_decode() has a depth limit of 512. If the data is deeper, it returns null (and json_last_error() says 'Maximum stack depth exceeded'). decodeJson() treats null as bad input, so the user gets a clear 422, not a crash.

title: The ??= operator sets a value only if the variable is null. What does this print?
explain: $a is null, so the first ??= sets it to 5. The second ??= does nothing, because $a is not null any more. Good for default values.

title: includes and indexOf treat NaN in different ways. What does Node print?
explain: includes() uses the SameValueZero rule, so NaN equals NaN. indexOf() uses strict equality, where NaN is never equal to anything, so it gives -1. Prefer includes() for a yes/no check.

title: After a rebase of your own feature branch you must force-push. Which command is safer?
explain: --force-with-lease refuses to push if someone added new commits to the remote branch since your last fetch. Plain --force would delete their work without a warning.
